name: [SVF2019] NGC 4736-1
description: A luminous blue variable in the galaxy M94, about three million times as luminous as the Sun.

radius.source: Solovyeva et al. (2019), MNRAS 484, L24, section 3.1: log(L_bol/L_sun) = 6.5 +/- 0.2 (at the paper's distance modulus of M94, 28.31) and T = 18 +/- 3 kK, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolution B3, Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788); the paper prints no radius, and no measurement of this star's size exists

temperature.source: Solovyeva et al. (2019), MNRAS 484, L24, section 3.1: photosphere temperature T = 18 +/- 3 kK, estimated from the strengths of its He I and Fe II lines

gravityRange.source: Clark et al. (2012), A&A 541, A145, table 4 (the model gravities of the four Galactic early-B hypergiants it analyses, at 13.7 to 18.1 kK, stars it finds intermediate between B supergiants and luminous blue variables)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M94, the star's galaxy, from 1999PASP..111..438F; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M94 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 4,337,391 pc (src/objects/m94-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 4,337,106 pc, inclination 31.77 deg, line of nodes 105 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, table 2 (distances of individual galaxies), PGC 43495: distance modulus 28.186 ± 0.039 mag (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94)

position.credit: Solovyeva et al. (2019), MNRAS 484, L24, section 2 (its HST coordinates, 12:50:57.264 +41:07:23.13); SIMBAD holds that position, from 2019MNRAS.484L..24S

text.card: A luminous blue variable in the galaxy M94, about three million times as luminous as the Sun.
text.introduction: Solovyeva et al. (2019) found it by its spectrum and saw its light change by 1.1 magnitudes from 2005 to 2018. They estimate its temperature at 18,000 K.
text.locator: section 3.1, NGC 4736_1: T, log(L_bol/L_sun), Delta V

notes: The star varies; it is drawn at the radius its published luminosity and temperature give
Its radius is not measured: it follows from the paper's luminosity and temperature
Its limb is read at the gravities published for early-B hypergiants; no gravity of this star is measured
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M94 is not measured
